newsitem.title: FRANCE: Snow may slow maize harvest in eastern France.
newsitem.headline: Snow may slow maize harvest in eastern France.

text.p: Early snow may slow the pace of the maize harvest in eastern France but does not threaten crop quality, local crop analysts said on Tuesday.
Snow, wind and rain has hit the Lorraine, Alsace, Jura and France-Comte regions.
"At this stage the snow is no threat to the crop but it may delay fieldwork by a few days," a local grain authoryt analyst in Strasbourg said.
The Alsace area, which is France's third maize producer after the Aquitaine and Midi-Pyrenees regions, was covered by a thin white layer following Monday's snowfall, he said.
"It snowed throughout Monday but the area received only between one and four inches," the analyst said.
Forecasters predict new snowfalls on Tuesday.
The main concern was that further snow or rain may keep farmers away from the fields and make grain movement more difficult, the analyst said.
In eastern France the maize harvest is 80-85 percent complete and had been expected to finish by end-November.
On Monday, local crop analysts said they had revised down yield estimates to 9.0 tonnes from the 9.2 tonnes they predicted two weeks ago. This would compare with 8.9 tonnes last year.
They explained that maize suffered from dry conditions in the summer while cool temperatures in the autumn slowed down plant development.
The regional maize area is thought to have risen to 126,00 hectares from 115,000 hectares last year.
